closed.reason: The verse is a bare greeting to Ampliatus as Paul's beloved in the Lord; Ampliatus appears nowhere else, and the other passages merely call other people or groups "beloved," which is a common epistolary term.

The verse greets five otherwise unknown men and the brothers with them; none of these names recurs for the same people (Hermes in Acts is the name of the god applied to Paul), and the other passages use "brothers" only in general address.

The verse greets Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas and the saints with them, none of whom appears elsewhere; the other passages offer only general greetings to saints or brothers, with no shared person.
